title: Zaidi Pushes Militia Disarmament Deadline to June 2027 After Meeting Rubio at UNGA
detail: PM Ali al-Zaidi met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, where the two 'agreed on the importance of Iraq dismantling terrorist militias' and Iraq exercising full sovereignty. Zaidi confirmed to the New York Times that the deadline to bring all non-state weapons under state control has been pushed from September 30, 2026 to June 2027, after hardline factions largely refused to comply. September 30 now marks only the end of the US-led coalition's mission, not the disarmament deadline. Zaidi called the effort 'not something that is optional. It is a necessity,' while an Iraqi official acknowledged 'significant resistance from militia groups.'

media.caption: Iraqi PM Ali Al Zaidi meets US Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the UN General Assembly

title: Iraq Recasts Sept 30 as Start of Plan to Collect 6 Million Weapons Nationwide
detail: Deputy Interior Minister Hussein al-Awadi described Iraq's plan to collect an estimated 6 million weapons held by non-state armed factions as 'the start of a regulatory process rather than a completion point,' effectively retreating from the original hard September 30 deadline. Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat al-Nujaba — the two hardline Tehran-aligned factions with histories of attacking US forces and Gulf states — refused to surrender what they call 'resistance weapons'; Kataib Hezbollah leader Abu Hussein al-Hamidawi vowed the group would instead 'develop them and expand its arsenal.' By contrast, Saraya al-Salam formally integrated into Iraqi security forces in a June 2026 Samarra ceremony, and Asaib Ahl al-Haq and Kataib Imam Ali have agreed to surrender or regularize their weapons. PM Zaidi said Iraq has 'no intention of using military means,' while a four-member committee including Zaidi and former PM Mohammed Shia al-Sudani develops revised mechanisms; the Trump administration has linked Iraq's compliance to its access to dollar flows.

media.caption: Members of the Shia Saraya al-Salam militia hand over weapons to Iraqi state forces in Samarra

title: Iraq's Oil Ministry Clarifies September Exports Averaged 2.6M bpd, Not 4M
detail: Iraq's Ministry of Oil clarified that crude exports averaged 2.6 million barrels per day (bpd) during September, after media reports mischaracterized a single day's peak SOMO shipment — 4 million bpd of crude routed outside the closed Strait of Hormuz — as the sustained monthly rate. Exports blended Qayara field crude via the northern outlet with southern port loadings and tanker shipments routed around Hormuz. The ministry called the 2.6M bpd average 'a significant achievement given current conditions, including the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz,' saying exports are 'being maintained at the highest possible levels to generate revenue for the state treasury.'
